title: WONTFIX candidate: validate_delegate_responder_cert's producedAt boundary
description:
## Why not

RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 requires a delegated responder certificate to have been
valid when the response was produced. `validate_delegate_responder_cert`
enforces it as

    if produced_at_unix < nb || produced_at_unix > na

and three mutants survive: `<` to `==`/`<=` and `>` to `>=`. Killing any of
them needs `producedAt` to equal a certificate validity edge exactly.

`producedAt` is set by the signing library at signing time, and the
certificate is embedded in the response it signs, so a generator cannot
know the value before it has built the thing that carries it. Landing on
equality would take an iterate-until-stable loop -- build, read producedAt,
rebuild the certificate with that notBefore, rebuild the response, repeat
until the timestamp stops moving -- and the resulting fixture would encode
one wall-clock second as a validity edge.

The guard's existence is already tested: `ocsp-delegated-expired-cert.der`
is a responder certificate whose validity ends before producedAt. What is
unpinned is only exactness at the boundary, and the consequence is a
one-second window either side of a certificate's validity.

## Decision

Not worth a bespoke generator. Filed so the three survivors are accounted
for rather than looking like an oversight on the next sweep, and so the
reasoning is here if someone disagrees.

Reopen if a cheap way to control `producedAt` appears -- a signing path that
takes it as a parameter would make this three lines of test.

## Found by

The first pkix-revocation mutation sweep, 2026-11-27.
close_reason:
Not a WONTFIX. Closed by 081356ea; all three mutants hand-verified killed.

My reasoning for filing it was wrong in a specific way worth recording: I argued producedAt had to be OBSERVED -- set by the signing library at signing time, unknowable before the response exists -- and concluded it would take an iterate-until-stable loop to land on a validity edge. It does not have to be observed, it can be WRITTEN. Build the response, rebuild its ResponseData at the DER level with producedAt replaced, re-sign with the responder key the generator holds. That is the same surgery dup-ext/gen.py has used since it needed a certificate cryptography refuses to emit, and I had used it twice the same day.

tests/fixtures/ocsp-produced-at/: four responses over two responder certificates, each pair one second apart in producedAt and identical otherwise. gen.py checks each spliced response parses, carries the producedAt asked for, and verifies under its own embedded certificate.

The lesson generalises: when a fixture needs a field the builder will not set, the question is not whether the builder can be coaxed into setting it but whether the field is inside something this generator can re-sign.
